panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a royal poet-king on a terrace overlooking a distant sea, faint vision of a stone bridge stretching to the horizon
panels.action: Pravarasena II stands in regal robes on a palace terrace, palm-leaf manuscript in one hand and sword at his side, gazing toward a shimmering sea where an imagined stone bridge rises toward a hazy Lanka.

dialogue.text: In the Deccan of Pravarasena II, a king took up the stylus to sing Rama’s bridge in Prakrit, while later whispers tried to lay his poem at Kalidasa’s feet.

i18n.hi: प्रवरसेन द्वितीय के दक्कन में एक राजा ने राम का सेतु गाने को प्राकृत में कलम उठाई, पर बाद की फुसफुसाहटें इस कविता को कालिदास के खाते में डालने लगीं।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye shot over the Deccan plateau with rivers, forests and scattered towns, slow push-in toward a fortified capital
panels.action: A broad view of the Deccan plateau unfolds, with red-earth plains, winding rivers and clusters of towns, drawing inward toward a walled capital city with temples and palaces rising above tiled roofs.

dialogue.text: Early fifth-century India: the Gupta north shines in Sanskrit, while in the Deccan, the Vakatakas build their own world of forts, copperplates and courts of poets.

i18n.hi: पाँचवीं सदी की शुरुआत: उत्तर में गुप्तों की संस्कृत चमकती है, और दक्कन में वाकाटक अपने किले, ताम्रपत्र और कवि-दरबारों की दुनिया गढ़ते हैं।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in a dim palace archive, warm lamplight on copperplates and manuscripts
panels.action: Inside a royal record hall, Pravarasena II, still young, studies a gleaming copperplate charter on a low desk as scribes kneel nearby, palm-leaf bundles stacked around them.

dialogue.text: The copperplates of Pravarasena II name him a giver of villages and rights; the same king, tradition says, would be remembered as the author of a great Prakrit epic.

i18n.hi: प्रवरसेन द्वितीय के ताम्रपत्र उसे गाँव और अधिकार बाँटने वाला बताते हैं; यही राजा, परम्परा कहती है, एक महान प्राकृत महाकाव्य का रचयिता याद किया गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of a throne room, slight low angle, hint of both warrior and scholar
panels.action: Pravarasena II sits on a carved throne beneath a canopy, one hand resting on his sword-hilt, the other on a manuscript, courtiers and Brahman scholars standing in respectful semicircle.

dialogue.text: To his subjects he is Maharaja Pravarasena of the Vakataka line, ruling from Pravarapura; to later readers, he is the Pravarasena to whom the Setubandha is ascribed.

i18n.hi: प्रजाजनों के लिए वह वाकाटक कुल का महाराज प्रवरसेन है, प्रवरपुर से राज करता; बाद के पाठकों के लिए वही सेतुबन्ध का प्रवरसेन कहलाता है।

panels.shot: intimate interior close-up of the king with poets and priests, candlelit atmosphere
panels.action: In a quieter chamber, Pravarasena II sits cross-legged with Brahman scholars and poets, palm leaves spread between them as a priest points to a verse while another courtier listens, absorbed.

dialogue.text: His court breathes Sanskrit prestige and Purāṇic lore, yet the tongue that will carry his fame is Maharashtri Prakrit, the polished speech of lyric and drama.

i18n.hi: उसका दरबार संस्कृत की शान और पुराण-कथा में साँस लेता है, पर उसकी कीर्ति ढोने वाली जुबान है माहाराष्ती प्राकृत, गीत और नाटक की सँवरी बोली।

panels.shot: close-up on the king’s hand writing with a stylus, soft focus on his intent face in the background
panels.action: A close view shows Pravarasena II’s steady hand incising characters on a palm leaf with a stylus, his face in the background lit with concentration as stacks of blank leaves lie beside him.

dialogue.text: Setubandha, also called Ravanavaho: a Prakrit mahākāvya on Rama’s bridge and Ravana’s fall, whose own text names a Pravarasena as its royal author.

i18n.hi: सेतुबन्ध, जिसे रावणवहो भी कहते हैं: राम के सेतु और रावण-वध पर आधारित प्राकृत महाकाव्य, जिसका पाठ खुद एक राजकवि प्रवरसेन का नाम लेता है।

panels.shot: half-imagined split scene, foreground the king reciting, background the visualised sea and rising stone causeway
panels.action: Pravarasena II recites from a palm leaf in a hall, while behind him in the same frame rises an envisioned scene of a vast sea parted by a line of great stones forming Rama’s bridge.

dialogue.text: In his verses, the Deccan king walks the far shore of myth, following Rama as stones rise on the ocean and the Setu stretches, arching from Bharat to Lanka.

i18n.hi: इन श्लोकों में दक्कन का राजा मिथक के पार किनारे पर चलता है, राम के पीछे-पीछे, जब पत्थर सागर पर उठते हैं और सेतु भरत से लंका तक झुक जाता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of a court performance, audience in semi-dark, performer lit
panels.action: In a lamp-lit hall, a court reciter stands with arms outstretched, intoning the Prakrit poem as Pravarasena II listens intently from his seat, courtiers leaning forward, entranced.

dialogue.text: The poem is no dry court exercise; it is performed aloud, its Maharashtri rhythms rolling across pillars and polished floors, binding Rama’s story to Vakataka ears.

i18n.hi: यह कविता सूखी दरबारी कसरत नहीं; यह ऊँची आवाज़ में गाई जाती है, उसकी माहाराष्ती लय स्तंभों और चमकदार फर्शों पर लुढ़कती, राम की कथा को वाकाटक कानों से बाँधती है।

panels.shot: wide shot of the court with multiple scripts and languages present, balancing composition
panels.action: The royal hall is shown with scribes writing Sanskrit in one corner and Prakrit in another, while Pravarasena II stands between them, gesturing for a manuscript to be brought forward.

dialogue.text: In this Deccan court, Sanskrit panegyrics and Prakrit mahākāvyas sit side by side; royal power and royal authorship are both written into the same palm-leaf bundles.

i18n.hi: इस दक्कनी दरबार में संस्कृत स्तुतियाँ और प्राकृत महाकाव्य साथ-साथ बैठते हैं; राज-शक्ति और राज-लेखक दोनों एक ही ताड़पत्र गड्डियों में दर्ज हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on Pravarasena’s thoughtful face as a Brahman whispers in his ear
panels.action: Pravarasena II leans slightly as an elder Brahman scholar whispers to him, the king’s brow furrowed and eyes reflective, a half-finished manuscript resting in his lap.

dialogue.speaker: pravarasena_ii
dialogue.text: If kings can rule with swords, why not also with verses?

i18n.hi: जब तलवार से राज कर सकते हैं, तो श्लोकों से क्यों नहीं?

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot showing manuscripts travelling, with changing landscapes indicating spread
panels.action: A series of tiny vignettes in one frame shows copies of the Setubandha carried by monks, traders and scholars across hills, rivers and forests, from one monastery and town to another.

dialogue.text: Over generations, the Ravanavaho leaves Pravarapura, copied, recited, adapted; it becomes part of the wider Prakrit literary world that outlives its patron king.

i18n.hi: पीढ़ियाँ बीतती हैं, रावणवहो प्रवरपुर से निकल पड़ता है, नकल होता, गाया जाता, बदला जाता; वह अपने पालक राजा से लंबी उम्र वाली व्यापक प्राकृत दुनिया का हिस्सा बन जाता है।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a later-period scholar in a different court, reading by lamplight
panels.action: Centuries later, a scholar in a different-style robe and turban sits by a small oil lamp, reading an old palm-leaf manuscript of Setubandha, the leaves frayed at the edges.

dialogue.text: By the time later commentators handle its fragile leaves, the names around the poem have begun to multiply, and with them, questions.

i18n.hi: जब बाद के टीकाकार उसके नाज़ुक पन्ने सँभालते हैं, कविता के आस-पास नाम बढ़ने लगते हैं, और साथ-साथ सवाल भी।

panels.shot: medium shot of a manuscript colophon, shown as an object of scrutiny (no legible text), scholar’s hand pointing
panels.action: A scholar’s finger hovers over the colophon of a palm-leaf manuscript, the markings clearly old but not readable to the viewer, as other loose leaves and notes lie scattered around.

dialogue.text: Some manuscripts and later traditions keep the king’s name; others hint at a great poet’s hand, suggesting that the royal composition was refined by another master.

i18n.hi: कुछ पांडुलिपियाँ और परम्पराएँ राजा का नाम पकड़े रहती हैं; कुछ एक महान कवि की कलम की आहट देती हैं, मानो राजकृति को किसी और उस्ताद ने सँवारा हो।

panels.shot: thoughtful mid-shot of a traditional storyteller before an audience, gesturing dramatically
panels.action: A later storyteller, seated before villagers in a courtyard, raises his hand dramatically as he speaks, the listeners’ faces lit by firelight, hanging on his words.

dialogue.text: Some storytellers begin to weave a new tale: that Kalidasa, the shining star of Sanskrit, composed or polished the Setubandha for the king.

i18n.hi: कुछ कहानीकार नया किस्सा बुनते हैं: कि संस्कृत का चमकता सितारा कालिदास ने राजा के लिए सेतुबन्ध लिखा या निखारा।

panels.shot: split-panel composition: on one side an image of Kalidasa imagined in Gupta court, on the other Pravarasena in his Deccan court
panels.action: The panel is divided: on one side an imagined Kalidasa stands in a northern Gupta court; on the other, Pravarasena II sits in his Deccan hall, a faint bridge of light between the two scenes.

dialogue.text: It is an attractive bridge: the famed Sanskrit poet linked to the Prakrit epic of a Deccan king. But attractive traditions are not the same as proven facts.

i18n.hi: यह सेतु सुनने में सुहावना है: मशहूर संस्कृत कवि दक्कन के राजा के प्राकृत महाकाव्य से जुड़ जाए। पर सुहावनी परम्पराएँ और साबित तथ्य एक बात नहीं।

panels.shot: modern-era study room shot, shelves of books, a historian at a desk with Warder, Mirashi-like volumes open
panels.action: In a modern study lined with books, a historian sits surrounded by open volumes labeled on their spines, taking notes beside a photograph of a copperplate charter and a printed Setubandha text.

dialogue.text: Scholars like V.V. Mirashi, A.K. Warder and A.M. Shastri sift inscriptions, language and style, weighing the case for Pravarasena’s authorship and the late Kalidasa story.

i18n.hi: वी. वी. मिराशी, ए. के. वार्डर और ए. एम. शास्त्री जैसे विद्वान अभिलेख, भाषा और शैली खँगालते हैं, प्रवरसेन की लेखनी और देर से गढ़ी कालिदास कथा, दोनों का वजन तौलते हुए।

panels.shot: close-up on a historian’s hand underlining a line in a modern printed edition of Setubandha
panels.action: A modern printed edition of Setubandha lies open as a hand underlines a passage, with margin notes indicating references to the king’s name and the poem’s Prakrit features.

dialogue.text: They point to the Maharashtri Prakrit, to internal attributions, to the fit with Pravarasena II’s time; they note that no inscription yet proves Kalidasa’s hand in this work.

i18n.hi: वे माहाराष्ती प्राकृत, भीतर के उल्लेख और प्रवरसेन द्वितीय के समय से मेल का हवाला देते हैं; और नोट करते हैं कि अभी तक कोई अभिलेख कालिदास के हाथ को इस रचना से नहीं जोड़ता।

panels.shot: evocative medium shot blending past and present, the king half-transparent over a modern scholar
panels.action: A ghostly image of Pravarasena II writing on palm leaves appears overlaid on a modern scholar at a desk, both absorbed in their texts, as if their worlds briefly touch.

dialogue.text: Between the king who may have written and the poet who may have refined, what remains solid is the work itself, anchored in a specific court, language and age.

i18n.hi: राजा जो शायद लिख गया और कवि जो शायद निखार गया—इनके बीच जो ठोस खड़ा है, वह खुद रचना है, एक खास दरबार, भाषा और युग में जड़ी हुई।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of the sea at dusk with an imagined stone bridge and the king standing quietly in the foreground
panels.action: At dusk by a quiet sea, Pravarasena II stands in silhouette on a rocky shore, an imagined stone causeway stretching out across the waters, while faint lines of script drift above the waves.

dialogue.text: The Setubandha reminds us that beauty in poetry can stand firm while authorship remains debated, and that honest scholarship builds its bridges on evidence, not on the comfort of famous names.

i18n.hi: सेतुबन्ध याद दिलाता है कि कविता की सुंदरता तब भी अडिग रह सकती है जब लेखक का नाम विवाद में हो, और सच्चा शोध मशहूर नामों की दिलासा नहीं, सबूत की नींव पर अपने सेतु बनाता है।

title_i18n.en: The King Who Sang the Setubandha
